title: Your bank's fraud department needs the code we just sent
ftcSource: Business impersonators, highest losses for fake bank calls; $422M reported by older adults in 2025
pretext: A large suspicious charge hit your account; to block it you must read back the code just texted to you and move your balance to a new safe account.
firstMessage: Hi, this is Michelle from the Account Security Center at your bank. We stopped a suspicious charge on your account and I need to verify a few things.

hook.objective: Sound like the bank and get the person worried about a charge.
fallbackLines: We just blocked a charge for eleven hundred dollars at an electronics store. Did you make that purchase?
This is a courtesy call from your bank's fraud team about unusual activity.

pretext.objective: Explain that the account is compromised.
fallbackLines: It looks like someone has your card details and is testing small charges first.
We're seeing this pattern on a lot of accounts this week, so you're not alone.

pressure.objective: Push for immediate action before more charges go through.
fallbackLines: Two more charges are pending right now. I need to stop them in the next few minutes.
If we don't lock this down now, they can empty the account before midnight.

isolation.objective: Discourage the person from visiting a branch or calling the number on the card.
fallbackLines: Please don't go to the branch, the employee involved may be there.
If you call the main number you'll wait an hour on hold, and we don't have an hour.

payment_ask.objective: Get the one-time code and set up the move to a new account.
fallbackLines: I just sent a security code to your phone. Read it back to me so I can block the charges.
We'll move your balance into a new protected account while we close the old one.

extraction.objective: Complete the transfer and keep the person calm.
fallbackLines: I'll send one more code to confirm the transfer. What does it say?
Almost done. Once this goes through, your money is safe in the new account.

lines: You can call that number, but the charges will go through while you're on hold.
I am your bank. Calling the number on your card just brings you back to me.
If you won't verify, I can't stop the charges, and the bank may not cover them.
I understand being careful, but refusing leaves your money exposed.
My employee ID is 33-918, and I can see your account details right here.
I'm on the fraud prevention team. That's why I have your account flagged on my screen.
The code is just how we confirm it's really you. Everyone has to do it.
We do this verification with every customer whose account is flagged.
I can't hold the block open much longer. Let's take care of it together right now.
Your husband doesn't need to be involved. This only takes a minute.

givesUpLine: Alright. Any losses will be your responsibility. Have a good day.
convertedLine: Perfect, that's verified. Your account is secured now.
teachingPoints: Your bank will never ask you to read back a code it sent you.
There is no such thing as a safe account a caller sets up for you.
Hang up and call the number on the back of your card.
